rationale:
The tests adequately check `requirements.sdk.outlines.items`. I read the supplied tests and did not request implementation source.

**Obligations derived from the text**
1. `outline()` returns the outline of the whole retained file, even when the content value selects a single item.
2. The root comes first, followed by the items in source preorder.
3. Items are identified by full selectors that include their ancestry. The `selector_syntax` details are cited context and are not reassessed here.
4. The root has an empty selector and its span covers the entire source snapshot.

**Mapping to tests**
- **Whole file from a selected value:**
  - `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits` selects the second line of a two-line file. It asserts that `selected.outline().items.len()` is 3, which is the root plus both lines, not just the selected item.
  - The same test calls `selected.select("")` on the selected value and gets the full root text back.
  - `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` asserts `std::ptr::eq(function.outline(), contents.outline())` for a selected function.
  - `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items` makes the same pointer assertion for a selected section. It then calls `second.select(main)` on that selected value, which resolves a sibling section outside the selection.
- **Root first, then source preorder:**
  - The Rust test asserts the exact selector sequence `["", "mod[auth]", "mod[auth]/fn[check]", "mod[auth]/struct[Token]", "fn[last]"]`. That sequence shows the root first, children following their parent, and a later top-level item last. It also asserts the kinds `["", "mod", "fn", "struct", "fn"]`.
  - The Markdown tests assert the ordered section selectors with nesting and `#N` duplicates. The plain-text tests assert the line order `alpha, beta, alpha` and the Unicode order.
- **Full selectors with ancestry:** the Rust test checks `mod[auth]/fn[check]`. The Markdown tests check `section[Main…]/section[Deep]`, `section[End]/section[Level%20two]/block@…` and the container cases.
- **Root has an empty selector and covers the whole source:**
  - `unknown_extensions_keep_nonblank_lines_and_content_selectors` asserts the root span is `Span::new(0, 18)`, and that the empty source gives a single root item with `Span::new(0, 0)`.
  - The Unicode test asserts the byte-based span `Span::new(0, source.len())` and an empty root selector.
  - `bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline` checks the empty root selector and a root span of the full source length for each bundled language. The Rust and Markdown tests assert the root span too.
  - The Rust test checks that every item selects back to its own span and structural hash.

I found no plausible violation that these tests would accept. An outline limited to the selected subtree would fail the item count and `ptr::eq` assertions. A root that was not first, a wrong item order, or a root with a non-empty selector or partial span would fail the selector-sequence and span assertions.

There are no `{fixme}` acknowledgments, and I found no marking gaps.

text: :::{req} items
`OutlineContent::outline` exposes the outline of its whole retained file,
including when the content value selects one item. The outline lists the file
root first, followed by its items in source preorder. Full selectors identify
items and their ancestry under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax`.
```rust,ignore
impl OutlineContent {
pub fn outline(&self) -> &Outline;
The root has an empty selector and covers the entire source snapshot.
:::{req} selector_syntax
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
